description: The Hacker’s Den is a team of problem-solvers driven to tackle complex space and Earth challenges with creativity, data, and technology. We combine skills in coding, science, and design to build practical solutions.
summary: NASA Field Shift is an agro-climatic decision support system for farmers, agronomists and planners in Pakistan and other arid-to-sub-humid regions. Given only coordinates and a date, a model built on the NASA-IBM Prithvi EO-V2 300M encoders predicts 16 variables: weather, soil moisture at four depths (5, 15, 50 and 150 cm), air quality and flood risk. A decision engine turns these into a Crop-Climate Resilience Score (A+ to F), crop recommendations from a 549-species FAO/NASA catalog, four crop rotation scenarios, a climate what-if simulator, and Urdu and English farmer advisories. It addresses the problem of farmers making planting and irrigation choices with scattered, hard-to-use data. Temperature R-squared is 0.968, and all 13 automated tests pass.
details:
What does it do, and how does it work?

NASA Field Shift takes a field location (latitude and longitude) and a date, and returns a full agro-climatic assessment through a web dashboard and a guided command-line wizard.

The NASA-IBM Prithvi EO-V2 LocationEncoder and TemporalEncoder turn position and time into 64-dimensional sinusoidal embeddings each.

These are combined with 9 cyclic features (hour, day of year and month) into a 137-dimensional input, which passes through residual blocks with LayerNorm and GELU.

Task-specific heads predict 16 variables: weather, soil water at four depths (5, 15, 50 and 150 cm), air quality index and flood risk.

A decision engine converts these into a Crop-Climate Resilience Score (A+ to F), a flood risk score, crop recommendations from a 549-species FAO/NASA catalog, four crop rotation scenarios, a climate what-if simulator and Urdu and English farmer advisories.

Google Gemini 2.5 Flash writes a feasibility report. If the API is unavailable, a built-in rule engine modeled on Pakistan Agricultural Research Council guidelines takes over.

What benefits does it have?

Farmers get one clear recommendation instead of using separate weather, soil, flood and air-quality tools. The system warns about flooding and smog, advises on irrigation, and suggests crops and rotations that fit current conditions. Advice is delivered in Urdu and English.

What is the intended impact?

The aim is better planting and irrigation decisions, which protect yield, reduce water waste and improve resilience to floods, drought and winter smog. It is built for Pakistan, and it can extend to other arid-to-sub-humid regions.

What tools, languages, hardware and software did you use?

Python, PyTorch, scikit-learn (gradient boosted ensemble), NumPy, pandas, SciPy, SQLite

Leaflet.js, Tailwind CSS and Font Awesome for the dashboard

NASA data: Prithvi EO-V2, POWER, GIBS, SMAP, GPM IMERG, MODIS, Landsat 8/9 and ECOSTRESS

Other data and services: AccuWeather, Meteomatics, FAO EcoCrop and Google Gemini 2.5 Flash

Runs on a standard PC with Python 3.10 or newer. One command (run.bat or run.sh) sets it up.

How is your project creative?

We pair a geospatial foundation model’s coordinate and time encoders with a farmer-facing decision layer. The system adds a resilience grade, rotation scenarios and a what-if simulator that matches a climate shift to a real analog city in Pakistan. Advice is delivered in the farmer’s own language, and the data is protected by a hardware-bound encrypted vault.

What factors did your team consider?

Physical realism: outputs are bounded (humidity 0–100%, soil water 0–0.6 m³/m³).

Reliability: the system falls back to a solar-cycle temperature model and a rule engine when APIs fail or are throttled.

Local conditions: the system accounts for seasonal smog around Lahore, Gujranwala and Faisalabad, and for each city’s flood vulnerability.

Accessibility: farmers get plain-language advice in Urdu and English.

Security: PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 with 200,000 rounds and tamper-evident records.

Validation: temperature R² of 0.968 with a 1.21 °C mean absolute error, and all 13 automated tests passing.

SI disclosure: Google Gemini 2.5 Flash generates runtime feasibility reports in the app. The NASA-IBM Prithvi EO-V2 encoders are used in the prediction model. The demo deck and submission text were drafted with Claude (Anthropic) and reviewed by the team. No images, audio or video are SI-generated.
